sprint: Image Studio Ship B — UX Refinement: sub-panels overlay + right-pane no-scroll. Sub-panels (`.picture-studio-subpanels` wrapping brush's Before⇄After/thickness/Undo/Redo controls, and crop's aspect-ratio/apply controls) are reparented from `_editPanel.appendChild(subWrap)` (inside the scrollable right column, where they were competing for the same 720px viewport space as the always-visible primary tiles + kid zoom slider + peek + reset + magic overlay controls) to `_stage.appendChild(subWrap)` — the already-`position:relative` stage acts as the containing block for a new absolute-positioned bottom overlay. CSS: `.picture-studio-subpanels` becomes `position:absolute; left:12px; right:12px; bottom:12px; z-index:9; pointer-events:none;` (a transparent hit-through container so a brush stroke started on the canvas above still lands correctly); the per-tool active state (`data-active-tool='brush'` / `'crop'`) reveals the matching `.picture-studio-subpanel[data-tool='...']` as `display:flex` with a translucent kid-friendly floating card (`background:rgba(255,251,240,0.94); border:1px solid rgba(255,203,69,0.55); border-radius:14px; padding:12px 14px; box-shadow:0 6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.15); backdrop-filter:blur(6px); pointer-events:auto;`) — a real, always-accessible-inside-the-stage secondary control surface, structurally guaranteed never to force the right pane to scroll. Cache-bust bumped ?v=0312→?v=0313 across every script/link tag in root index.html.
task: Two directly-verifiable outcomes: (1) `.picture-studio-edit-view`'s own scrollHeight === clientHeight (no scroll on the right pane) at both a comfortable 900px viewport and a shorter 700px viewport, since the sub-panels no longer occupy right-pane vertical space at all; (2) the brush sub-panel's rendered rect sits genuinely inside `.picture-studio-stage`'s own bounds (not just "present in DOM") — pointer-events:auto so a real click on Before/After/thickness/Undo/Redo works, translucent 94% opacity so the brush stroke content beneath it stays partially visible, backdrop-filter:blur(6px) so it reads as a floating overlay rather than an opaque bar cutting the stage. Verified via a new 13-assertion Playwright suite (scratch-only, `subpanels_overlay_verify.js`) driving the Ship B modal end-to-end: setup (fixture image via HTMLImageElement, PictureStudio.open, wait for edit view), then sample each of `_stage.contains(subWrap)`, subWrap.parentElement.className, brush sub-panel's computed `display`/`position`/`pointerEvents`/`backgroundColor` when Brush tile is `data-active-tool='brush'`, `.picture-studio-subpanels` wrapper's own computed `position`/`bottom`/`zIndex`/`pointerEvents`, brush sub-panel's `getBoundingClientRect()` genuinely inside stage's own `getBoundingClientRect()` (top≥stage.top-2 && bottom≤stage.bottom+2), edit view's scrollHeight===clientHeight at 900px viewport (720===720), and — the decisive second-viewport check — the same no-scroll invariant held at a shorter 700px viewport too. A real test-methodology bug was found and fixed during verification, not an app bug, disclosed rather than glossed over: an initial version of the verify script built its return object AFTER `modal.remove()`, but `getComputedStyle` returns a live `CSSStyleDeclaration` whose reads return empty strings for a detached element — 7 assertions failed with empty details even though the app-side CSS was correct. Traced via 3 diagnostic scripts confirming the same probe structure returned correct values in isolation, then a temporary `console.log(JSON.stringify(probe))` dump inside the verify itself. Fixed by building `const result = {...}` snapshot BEFORE `modal.remove()` — the fix restored all 7 CSS-reading assertions to passing, 13/13 clean. Cache-bust bumped ?v=0312→?v=0313 uniformly across every script/link tag in root index.html so a returning browser's cache is guaranteed to re-fetch the modified CSS.
